questions.question: Which civilization is described as the oldest in the Americas and one of the first six independent civilizations in the world?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the Norte Chico civilization in Peru dating back to about 3500 BC is the oldest civilization in the Americas and one of the first six independent civilizations in the world.
Incorrect. The article says the Norte Chico predated the Mesoamerican Olmec by nearly two millennia, meaning the Olmec came later.
Incorrect. The Muisca are described as one of the four grand civilisations in the Americas but not as the oldest.
Incorrect. The Inca are mentioned in relation to their conquest of the CaÃ±ari, not as the oldest civilization in the Americas.

questions.question: Which two European powers are identified as having colonized South America and disrupted indigenous life?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that indigenous peoples' thousands of years of independent life were disrupted by European colonization from Spain and Portugal.
Incorrect. The article does not mention England or France as colonizers disrupting indigenous life in South America.
Incorrect. Spain is named, but England is not identified as a colonizer of South America in the article.
Incorrect. Portugal is named, but France is not identified as a colonizer disrupting indigenous life in South America.

questions.question: What was the approximate date of the Monte Verde II site in Chile, among the oldest evidence for human presence in South America?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that amongst the oldest evidence for human presence in South America is the Monte Verde II site in Chile, suggested to date to around 14,500 years ago.
Incorrect. Around 13,000 years ago is when the Fishtail projectile point style became widespread, not the date of Monte Verde II.
Incorrect. Around 11,000 years ago is when the Fishtail projectile point style disappeared, not the date of Monte Verde II.
Incorrect. Circa 6500 BC is the date for the first evidence of agricultural practices, not the Monte Verde II site.

questions.question: Which animals were domesticated by South American cultures in the highlands of the Andes circa 3500 BC?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that South American cultures began domesticating llamas and alpacas in the highlands of the Andes circa 3500 BC.
Incorrect. Guinea pigs were domesticated as a food source at this time, but cattle are not mentioned as domesticated animals in the article.
Incorrect. Horses and sheep are not mentioned as animals domesticated by South American cultures circa 3500 BC.

Incorrect. Llamas were domesticated circa 3500 BC, but guinea pigs are mentioned separately as also being domesticated as a food source at this time, not paired with llamas as the primary domesticated animals.

questions.question: What geological event approximately 3 million years ago connected South America to North America?
options: the formation of the Panamanian land bridge
the separation of Antarctica and South America
the divergence of South America and Africa along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that approximately 3 million years ago, South America became connected to North America when the Bolivar Trough marine barrier disappeared and the Panamanian land bridge formed.
Incorrect. Antarctica and South America separated during the late Eocene, around 35 mya, which is much earlier than 3 million years ago.
Incorrect. The CretaceousâPaleogene extinction event occurred 66 Mya and is associated with dinosaur mass-extinction, not the connection of the Americas.
Incorrect. South America and Africa began to diverge in the Albian around 110 mya, which is much earlier than 3 million years ago.

questions.question: Which species is identified as the first known to have made the northward migration during the Great American Interchange?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the first species known to have made the northward migration was Pliometanastes, a fossil ground sloth roughly the size of a modern black bear.
Incorrect. Megatherium is listed among species that followed the route north during the Irvingtonian stage around 1.9 mya, not as the first species.
Incorrect. Titanis is described as the terror bird that dispersed into North America, but not as the first species to migrate northward.
Incorrect. Pampatherium is listed among species that followed the route north during the Irvingtonian stage around 1.9 mya, not as the first species.

questions.question: What percentage of present-day South American mammals does the article say have evolved from North American species?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that about 60% of present-day South American mammals have evolved from North American species.
Incorrect. The article does not state that about 30% of present-day South American mammals evolved from North American species.
Incorrect. The article does not state that about 90% of present-day South American mammals evolved from North American species.
Incorrect. The article does not state that about 10% of present-day South American mammals evolved from North American species.

questions.question: Which of the following is described as a characteristic of the Caral Supe complex?
options: It had absolutely no signs of warfare.
It was dependent on agriculture rather than fishing.
It was located in present-day Ecuador.
It was contemporaneous with the Mesoamerican Olmec.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the Caral Supe complex is noteworthy for having absolutely no signs of warfare.
Incorrect. The article states that the Norte Chico civilization is believed to have been the only civilization dependent on fishing rather than agriculture.
Incorrect. The article states that the Caral-Supe civilization emerged on the north-western coast of present-day Peru, not Ecuador.
Incorrect. The article states that the Norte Chico civilization preceded the civilization of Mesoamerica by two millennia, meaning it was not contemporaneous with the Olmec.

questions.question: What role did Muisca women exclusively perform according to the article?
options: extraction of halite from brines in salt mines
leading military campaigns against the Spanish
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the extraction process of halite from brines in salt mines was the work of the Muisca women exclusively.
Incorrect. The article does not mention Muisca women leading military campaigns against the Spanish.
Incorrect. The article states that South American cultures domesticated llamas and alpacas in the Andes, but does not attribute this exclusively to Muisca women.
Incorrect. The article describes the Muisca as organised in a loose confederation of rulers, but does not state that women exclusively governed it.

questions.question: Which group is described as having repulsed the Incan invasion with fierce resistance for many years until they fell to Tupac Yupanqui?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the CaÃ±ari were most notable in having repulsed the Incan invasion with fierce resistance for many years until they fell to Tupac Yupanqui.
Incorrect. The Muisca are described as one of the four grand civilisations in the Americas, not as the group that resisted the Inca until falling to Tupac Yupanqui.
Incorrect. The Tairona are mentioned as located in present-day Colombia alongside the Muisca, but not as the group that resisted the Inca.
